transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I came in because... I just keep thinking it would be better if I didn't wake up. I go to sleep hoping I just stay that way. And honestly, sometimes I feel like dying would be the fair punishment for what I've done to my family, and to my crew at work. That's why I'm here.
Can you tell me more about what you feel you have done to your family and your crew?

I just... I keep thinking I'm the reason my husband got worse. And with work—I do flooring and tile—I'm the reason my crew lost out on jobs. I feel like I just messed up our clients' homes. It's like... like I've poisoned everything I touch. So, whatever happens to me, I deserve it.
Have you ever experienced a time before this where you felt severely depressed like this?

Well, I wouldn't say I've felt this way before. It's just been this one long stretch. The depression has been with me for about a year and two months now. It started a few months after my husband's injury, and it just hasn't lifted since.
Have you heard any voices or sounds when no one is around, or that other people couldn't hear?

Yes, actually. I've been hearing a man's voice. It usually happens when I'm at a job site, or sometimes when I'm just in my kitchen at home. It sounds like he's right behind me, clear as day, like someone is standing right there. He says things like, "You missed it," or "Everyone knows." But... whenever I turn around to look, there's nobody there.
